item.title: 🎙 Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s remarks on the 2026 elections to the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation
item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s remarks on the 2026 elections to the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation (Moscow, September 18, 2026) 💬 Sergey Lavrov: Dear friends, Voting is now underway to elect the ninth State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation. 🗳 On September 18-20, we are all called upon to make a choice of great importance to our country. In his address to Russian citizens , President of Russia Vladimir Putin stressed the significance of these elections for Russia’s future , its continued development, and the protection of its security and sovereignty. The President urged all of us to exercise our constitutional right and make a responsible choice , so that the election results demonstrate the maturity and resilience of Russian society. 👉 This will be our collective response to those who seek to weaken Russia and deny us the right to determine our own destiny. #Elections2026

item.content:encoded:

❓
Question:
NATO is under enormous strain, but far from broken. President Donald Trump has threatened US troop cuts and criticized allies over their defense spending and perceived lack of support for US war against Iran. Yet the U.S. continues to invest in key NATO military facilities and relies on them to project power globally. Many officials say transatlantic trust has slumped, weakening Article 5. How does Russia assess the situation?
💬
Answer:
Disagreements among the allies are strictly an internal NATO matter, and we do not consider it appropriate to comment on them. What we see is that the US makes Europe pay more and more on military needs regardless of the costs. NATO Secretary General M.Rutte is bragging almost every day about enormous military spending and boost in production of armaments and military equipment as if it were good for economies and societies. But the European statistics show that this is totally false –
stagnation, public debt, rising prices, deindustrialization, bankruptcies and decline in the standard of living are direct consequences of this reckless policy.
For Russia the most important point remains that, at the Ankara summit, Alliance members once again identified Russia as a long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic stability and security, while all military planning and force development within NATO are geared toward confrontation with us and preparations for war against us. In other words,
NATO has no will to learn any lessons from the crisis in European security that it created with its own hands, nor does it want to change its destructive course.
❗️
Russia has no intention to attack NATO countries or threaten the Alliance but we will do everything to protect our national security and to counter threats emanating from NATO.
❓
Question:
Trump's anti‑NATO rhetoric may signal to President Putin that the West is divided and more vulnerable than it appears. A wave of sabotage incidents across the continent, which European countries blame on Russia – including an attempted drone attack on a German airport, a fire at a Polish factory, recent drone incursions into Romania – have heightened those concerns. What is Your reaction to these accusations?
💬
Answer:
With all its escalatory behavior the Alliance is deliberately spreading scare stories about a supposedly looming Russian attack on NATO countries. This is done in order to justify forced militarization to the detriment of the region’s peaceful development and the socio-economic well-being of its citizens. Unfortunately, due to years of NATO and EU ‘brainwashing’ and scaremongering over a so-called Russian threat many citizens find it difficult to realize that
it is precisely the proponents of confrontation who are driving Europe into a dead end.
As for the incidents mentioned, we've repeatedly denied the baseless allegations of Russia's involvement.
They are nothing more than dirty provocations in the interests of the bankrupt Kiev regime and the European "war party"
, who are seeking at any cost to drag NATO and the EU into a direct conflict with Russia, with all the ensuing catastrophic consequences. In the same time, these incidents are obviously used in the domestic political struggle, as it is the case in Germany where the current government is stirring up a scandal trying to divert attention of the public from the weakening economy and raise its sagging ratings.
❓
Question:
A European former arms procurement minister said that it would be a mistake for European countries to abandon buying U.S.‑made F‑35 fighter jets, arguing that "the thing Putin is most afraid of is the F‑35s". How can You comment on this?
💬
Answer:
These statements are a perfect example of how Russia's imaginary threat is being exploited for opportunistic purposes. This time the Russian bugaboo is used to persuade Europeans to continue purchasing extremely expensive US military equipment.
🔗
Source:
Reuters

item.title: 📆 On September 2, a Russian woman who had been forcibly held at a scam call centre in Myanmar since June
item.description: 📆 On September 2, a Russian woman who had been forcibly held at a scam call centre in Myanmar since June returned home with the assistance of the Russian Embassy in Thailand . Despite the efforts of law enforcement authorities across South-East Asia, human trafficking for the subsequent involvement of victims in the activities of criminal organisations remains one of the most serious transnational threats in the region . In this regard, we would once again urge Russian citizens to exercise caution when approached by strangers seeking to establish contact via social networks and messenger s, as well as when responding to online advertisements for highly paid positions in tourism, administration, translation and modelling. ☝️ At the same time, we would like to stress that travelling to South-East Asian countries, including Myanmar and Thailand, for tourism purposes does not in itself pose a threat, provided that the above-mentioned security rules are observed.

item.title: ⚡️ The International Public Tribunal on the Crimes of Ukrainian Neo-Nazis has published a report
item.description: ⚡️ The International Public Tribunal on the Crimes of Ukrainian Neo-Nazis has published a report “Heirs of Goebbels: Falsification of the Events in Bucha and Bloody Staged Performances of the Kiev Regime” , presenting its findings on the Bucha hoax , and how the Kiev regime and its Western sponsors through mainstream media support falsified the events of what occurred in Bucha in 2022. The Tribunal brings together civil society representatives from 35 countries . Drawing on Ukrainian media reports, memorial records and eyewitness testimony, the publication debunks the claim that the individuals commemorated at the Bucha memorial were civilians killed by Russia's Armed Forces . Key findings: ▪️ Military personnel presented as civilian victims The report identifies Ukrainian servicemen and combatants listed among the memorial’s “civilian victims” . Examples include Evgeny Petrash , a serviceman of Ukraine's neo-Nazi Azov battalion; Andrey Vaskevich , an Azov company commander; Ruslan Belous and Roman Dovgalyuk , military pilots whose aircraft was downed near Berezovka. Other entries include a sniper of Ukraine's 80th separate air assault brigade Oleg Tsimbal , members of territorial defence units, airborne formations and military intelligence. ▪️ Discrepancies in the location and cause of death A number of people commemorated at the Bucha memorial died elsewhere . Ukrainian sources place the deaths of a number of servicemen near Vorzel, Moshchun, Kopylov and other settlements.

, presenting its findings on
the Bucha hoax
, and how the Kiev regime and its Western sponsors through mainstream media support falsified the events of what occurred in Bucha in 2022.
The Tribunal brings together civil society representatives from 35 countries
. Drawing on Ukrainian media reports, memorial records and eyewitness testimony, the publication
debunks the claim
that the individuals commemorated at the Bucha memorial were civilians killed by
Russia's Armed Forces
.
Key findings:
▪️
Military personnel presented as civilian victims
The report identifies
Ukrainian servicemen
and combatants
listed among the memorial’s
“civilian victims”
.
Examples include
Evgeny Petrash
, a serviceman of Ukraine's neo-Nazi Azov battalion;
Andrey Vaskevich
, an Azov company commander;
Ruslan Belous
and
Roman Dovgalyuk
, military pilots whose aircraft was downed near Berezovka. Other entries include a sniper of Ukraine's 80th separate air assault brigade
Oleg Tsimbal
, members of territorial defence units, airborne formations and military intelligence.
▪️
Discrepancies in the location and cause of death
A number of people commemorated at the Bucha memorial died elsewhere
. Ukrainian sources place the deaths of a number of servicemen near Vorzel, Moshchun, Kopylov and other settlements.
The report also cites
68-year-old Galina Semenyuk
,
who died of cancer
but somehow appears on the memorial. Such cases highlight the need to establish each person’s circumstances of death before presenting the entire list as
“civilian victims killed by the Russian military”
.
▪️
Witness accounts of shelling and manipulated coverage
The publication includes 16 witness accounts from Avdeevka, Ugledar, Dzerzhinsk and other towns and cities
. Witnesses recount Ukrainian attacks on residential areas followed by the arrival of journalists, coverage blaming Russia, and pressure on residents to repeat that account.
***
The Tribunal’s conclusion is unequivocal:
the material it has collected points to
blatant falsification of events in Bucha by the Kiev regime with Western support
, alongside a broader practice of killing civilians to produce footage blaming Russia.
☝️
The cases presented in this publication form only part of the evidence assembled by
the Tribunal
.

item.title: ✉️ On September 17, President of Russia Vladimir Putin sent a message to Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi, extending heartfelt congratulations on his birthday
item.description: ✉️ On September 17, President of Russia Vladimir Putin sent a message to Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi, extending heartfelt congratulations on his birthday . ✍️ Please accept my heartfelt congratulations on your birthday. You rightfully command great respect among your compatriots and enjoy considerable standing on the world stage. 🇷🇺 🇮🇳 Your personal contribution to strengthening the special and privileged strategic partnership between India and Russia can hardly be overstated. I would like to express my gratitude for the cordial welcome and generous hospitality extended to me and the Russian delegation during our visit to New Delhi last week. Our talks were undoubtedly substantive, frank and highly productive. As always, I sincerely enjoyed our conversations , which once again affirmed your exceptional political wisdom and foresight. We will, of course, continue working constructively together on pressing bilateral and international issues for the benefit of the friendly peoples of our countries. 🤝 I sincerely wish you, my dear friend, sound health, happiness, well-being and every success in your service to the nation. VLADIMIR PUTIN #RussiaIndia #DruzhbaDosti

🎙
Russia's President Vladimir Putin Address to the nation ahead of the 2026 State Duma elections
💬
Vladimir Putin
: Friends, citizens of Russia,
I consider it important to address you now, when our big country is going through a s
ignificant and largely definitive election campaign
.
In strict compliance with law and within the specified timeframe, we are electing members of the
State Duma, legislative assemblies, governors of several regions
, and members of
municipal bodies
.
This extensive election campaign is taking place as we continue the
special military operation
. Residents of
Donbass and Novorossiya
will be voting for State Duma deputies for the
first time since their reunification with Russia
.
I firmly believe that our soldiers and officers involved in this challenging work at the frontline will be among active voters. Their
courage and loyalty to the Fatherland are exemplary for the entire nation
.
We know what Russia is fighting for and what the duty of every citizen is
. Our heroes are forging victory on the battlefield. Everybody who is honestly working for the benefit of the country – and understand their responsibility for its future – are bringing this victory closer. Participation in the upcoming vote that is taking place during the Year of the
Unity of the Peoples of Russia
is also a responsibility and contribution to the country’s strength.
❗️
Your choice and determination will show once again that millions of people are backing our fighters and that we stand together, united by shared values, our historical memory, love for our Motherland, and that nobody can divide or intimidate us, undermine our statehood, our public and political system.
Every vote matters
. You and your personal choice will directly determine what political forces will represent people’s interests in the federal parliament, in the regions and in local governance.
I am certain that, with your support and trust,
the most deserving and competent candidates, the true patriots of Russia will come out as winners
. Those will be candidates who will not let you down and who have proved their loyalty to the Motherland and their readiness to serve our nation and protect our country from any threats.
Friends,
🗳
The voting will take place over three days, on September 18, 19 and 20.
I urge you to
exercise your constitutional right and make a thought-out and responsible decision
, so that the election results attest to the maturity and resilience of Russian society. This will be our collective response to those who seek to undermine Russia, slow down its development, or strip away our sovereignty or our right to determine our own future.
🇷🇺
Participation in the elections is our joint contribution to Russia’s victory.

🌐
Leadership in a Multipolar World: What Determines a Country’s Position in the New International Reality?
🟢
On September 15, as part of the
International Festival of Youth — 2026
, MGIMO hosted a panel discussion titled
“Leadership in a Multipolar World: What Determines a Country’s Position in the New Architecture of International Relations?”
Leading experts in international relations discussed the nature of leadership and the key factors shaping a country’s position on the global stage.
📩
The discussion was moderated by Stanislav Surovtsev
, Vice-Rector for International Cooperation, Youth and Social Policy, MGIMO University.
The panel brought together:
✅
Maria Zakharova
, Director of the Information and Press Department of the Russian MFA;
✅
Arno Gujon
, Director of the Office for Public and Cultural Diplomacy of the Government of the Republic of Serbia;
✅
Dauren Abayev
, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Kazakhstan to the Russian Federation.
✅
Toufik Djouama
, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the People’s Democratic Republic of Algeria to the Russian Federation.
Here are the key takeaways from the discussion
👇
⚪
Maria Zakharova
highlighted a number of leadership qualities that challenge conventional perceptions of what it means to be a leader.
“It is commonly believed that a leader is someone who is always ahead, someone who strives to take first place. This is a misconception.
Leadership is not about competition or being formally first. Leadership is strength and confidence that become a source of support for others.
Leadership is when you are targeted by a campaign against you, yet still find the strength to keep moving forward,” Maria Zakharova emphasized.
⚪
Dauren Abayev
stressed that
domestic stability
remains the foundation of an effective foreign policy: “Without stability within a country, it is impossible to act effectively on the international stage.” Speaking about cooperation between countries and continents, he put forward the principle that
“a bridge is more important than a fortress,”
emphasizing the importance of openness, connections and communication over isolation. Dauren Askerbekovich emphasized that
Russia and Kazakhstan are key strategic partners
.
⚪
Arno Gujon
emphasized that
leadership is made possible not by words, but by actions.
“We will not pursue a policy that treats Russia immorally. This is
a principled position based on values, not political expediency.”
⚪
Toufik Djouama
outlined a fundamental principle of genuine partnership:
“It begins where people not only take, but also share.”
According to him, this principle applies equally to relations between individuals and to cooperation between states.
➡️
We thank all speakers and participants for a meaningful dialogue that brought together diverse professional and national perspectives — and for the opportunity to discuss together what defines the leadership of states today and what the world of tomorrow may look like.
🌐
MGIMO International
(ENG) /
МГИМО для иностранцев
(RUS)
